name: map scenery props
fixDirection: Extrude the eleven prop kinds as small procedural meshes in GLGeometry and bake them into the map mesh in buildMapMesh from env.models, using the same authored x/y/size/rotation and the ul(x / AUTHORED_PX_PER_UL) conversion the zones already use. They go in the existing single map draw call at zero per-frame cost, and the reactor/coil/pylon kinds are where the first emissive ley geometry on the board belongs.

name: The Siphon (placeholder cylinder, no model)
fixDirection: It needs a model — write tools/blender/tower_siphon.py and export a real base body. Nothing else on this group is worth touching first; every other criterion is scoring at or near zero because there is no asset, and the interim cylinder cannot be improved into one.

name: Earthquake and floor fissures (Warbringer B5)
fixDirection: Port the quake into World3D at all: drive a real camera kick through OrbitCamera (offset the target, not a ctx.translate) and rebuild the fissures as projected ground polylines in drawEffects the way drawGroundRing already projects — and recolour them ember, because this is the Warbringer's ability, not the Sniper's.

name: The Tyrant - wave-35 campaign boss
fixDirection: Author a real Tyrant mesh - six of the eight criteria are hard-capped at 1 by the primitive and nothing else can move until it exists. Build it as the heavy DIRECTION describes: armoured chassis first, unnatural organic contamination visibly grown through the plating, red core emissive on the geometry - and in the same pass wire windUpTimer, the roar and the leap to uGlow on that model's own emissive parts plus a world-space GL telegraph, so the 1.3 s wind-up and the 120 u.l. shockwave stop being invisible.

name: The Siphon beam
fixDirection: Before any modelling work, draw the beams in World3D — a per-lock projected line from a spout anchor to the target, width driven by ramp and flowPower, is a dozen lines in drawEffects and turns an invisible tower into a working one.

name: Shield field and break pulse
fixDirection: Port the break pulse first, not the steady field — one gold projected ring expanding off the body on shieldFlash is a handful of lines in drawEffects, costs nothing per-frame because it only exists for half a second per break, and restores the single most informative state change the 3D renderer currently drops.

name: contact shadows and grounding
fixDirection: Ship one projected blob quad per actor on the ground plane, multiplicative rather than a canvas ellipse so it darkens the deck instead of painting over it. Everything needed is already there: a ground plane at z=0, GLMath.modelYaw for the transform, and GLModels.expand already walks every vertex to compute model.top, so it can compute a footprint radius in the same loop. At ~100 actors in the stress scene that is a few thousand fragments at 720p and well under 40k at 4K — a fraction of the ~3 ms of headroom PERF.md leaves unspent — and it is the single change that stops every actor in every capture from floating.

name: The sixteen enemy types with no model - coloured spheres
fixDirection: Replace the sphere primitive with a procedural faceted machine kit in GLGeometry - one chassis plus plate plus a lit red core slot, using the modelled enemies' tin/steel/red-core vocabulary and a real emissive buffer - parameterised off the Enemy.TYPES row so armour plates, camo shell, shield ring, healer mast and flight lift come out of data. That kills the one-silhouette-for-sixteen-types problem immediately, at a few hundred triangles each, without waiting on Blender.

name: Screen transitions (menu/chooser/play/index/armoury)
fixDirection: Add one shared transition state (outgoing screen id + eased 0..1 progress) that draw() honours for every screen, and start with the cheapest version that reads: a ~180ms eased crossfade plus a small scale or slide on the incoming screen, so no cut is ever a single-frame value jump.

name: emission / uGlow channel
fixDirection: Carry emission COLOUR per vertex instead of per draw, and delete the baked white floor. The palette already stores it as [r,g,b,emission] and expand() already reads it — add an aEmiCol attribute (or fold it into the existing colour path), stop adding min(1,emit*0.16) into the base colour, and make the term lit += vEmiCol * vEmi * (uRestGlow + uGlow). That single change kills the pure-white clamp, restores ember/violet/ley meaning without a tint uniform, lets an enemy core be red, and makes normalising the wild 0.58-to-7.0 authored range a one-pass rescale.

name: Health bars, enemies and towers
fixDirection: Separate the bars by value and by size before touching anything else: scale bar width with the body's radius, sit it on a dark plate that separates it from its neighbours, and re-hue off the traffic-light ramp so red stays enemy-only. Then add the two motion beats that make damage read — an eased fill and a lingering pale trail behind the loss.

name: shared material palette
fixDirection: Promote one palette to a real shared module that both pipelines and gl-world import — with the names DIRECTION.md already cites — and re-anchor the whole ladder against the board's measured lit value rather than against hex in isolation. The first concrete edit: the deck is authored #0c2633 but lights to 0.161 lum, brighter than most of every tower standing on it, so drop it into the 0.06-0.08 band; then demote the enemies' brass trim to a dark iron so the red core is the only bright note on an enemy and the reserved money gold stops appearing on hostile machinery.

name: Victory and game-over overlays
fixDirection: Build one shared button component in the menu's bracketed-keycap language and use it here, then give the ending a timeline: scrim fades in, title lands with a slight overshoot, stat lines reveal in sequence, and the coin payout counts up in gold -- motion 0->4 and effect 1->3 with no fill-rate cost.

name: Armoury / store screen
fixDirection: Cache the specimen instance per picked id instead of constructing one per frame, then spend the empty right two-thirds on a large render of the selected tower so the shop actually sells what it is charging 150 coins for.

name: The four tower icons
fixDirection: Kill the vector icons and generate all four from the same source as the Rifleman -- a fixed-camera crop of each tower's model, on a shared plinth, at a size that fits inside the slot above the label -- so the bar shows four people in one lighting model instead of two lollipops, a hammer and a photograph.

name: terrain slabs across all six maps
fixDirection: Fix the occlusion first — it is a two-number change that unlocks everything else. Make the metalDark box a RIM (drawn below the slab top, or as four edge boxes) instead of a solid cap that sits 0.1 u.l. proud of it, so P.panel actually renders. Then give the three zone kinds three distinct values (hazard warmest/accent-tinted, bay darkest, deck lightest, matching what drawZone already established in 2D) and push floor-to-slab separation past 20% relative luminance, not 7.6%.

name: board void / backdrop margin
fixDirection: Pass the map's own theme.background through to renderer.begin() as the clear colour so the six facilities stop sharing one void — it is a one-line change that immediately restores the map identity the 2D path already had, and it costs nothing against the fill-rate budget.

name: shader lighting model
fixDirection: Restore the third light. Pass the camera direction as a single per-frame uniform (the camera is a fixed tilted ortho-ish rig, so it costs one uniform and zero per-vertex work) and add a cool rim term such as pow(1 - max(dot(n,uViewDir),0), 3) * uRimColor, then pull uAmbient back toward the Blender reference (~0.06,0.09,0.14) so the rim has somewhere dark to sit. It is the only term in reach that can put an edge on an actor standing on a 0.161-luminance floor, and it is what td_scene.py already has and gl-renderer.js dropped.

name: Build bar
fixDirection: Fix the layout first — it is broken at the only size it is ever drawn: give the icon its own box that clips, drop the label below it, and make both towers' icons come from one renderer at one scale. Then re-skin the slot as a socket on the terminal (etched plate, ley trace along the armed edge in cyan not green, an explicit locked treatment for empty slots).

name: Inspection panel
fixDirection: Lay the panel out once on open and blit it from an offscreen canvas — that removes ~1.0 ms/frame and is the single cheapest win in this whole set. While rebuilding it, dock it to a screen edge so it stops burying the boss bar and the board, and give it a header band with the tower's portrait and tier so it stops reading as a debug dump.

name: Death burst
fixDirection: Stop sourcing the burst from type.color — drive it from the fixed table instead (red core matter plus neutral iron debris, mass-scaled by radiusPx) so a kill stops borrowing ley cyan, covenant violet and bounty gold, and add a short ground scorch so a kill outweighs a hit.

name: Pause menu
fixDirection: Share the menu's button component, fade the scrim in over ~150ms with an ease-out, and desaturate/darken the frozen board behind it rather than relying on a flat 82% wash.

name: pierce lance and its remnant
fixDirection: Delete the white head disc and rebuild beam() as a single stroke whose colour comes from a gradient ACROSS the width (white core -> ley -> transparent) via a rotated createLinearGradient, with tapered rather than butt ends. That removes the ball that reads as a bug, restores the value ladder (dark outside, hot inside) and cuts two of the three overdraw passes at the same time.

name: Boss bar
fixDirection: Give the bar a frame and a threat read — a plated housing, segment ticks so 9000 HP is countable, the enemy's silhouette at the left — and draw it after the inspection panel so a tower panel can never bury the boss. Re-hue off ritual magenta onto the palette's enemy red, and add the two beats it has none of: an entrance and an eased drain with a hit flash.

name: Index / field guide screen
fixDirection: Fill the dead lower half by making the tree an exhibit: show the tower rendered at the selected tier beside the path, and give each tier box a small silhouette plus a one-line effect so the grid stops being ten blank rectangles.

name: Hover cards
fixDirection: Colour the delta by sign — a negative change must not print green; that is a one-line fix and it is currently lying to the player. Then bring the enemy card up to the tower card's standard (name, type and traits, not just an HP figure) and give both a pointer to the body so the card stops floating free.

name: Status rings, stun indicator, kill stacks
fixDirection: Split the stun countdown off the stun ring by value, not distance — keep the ring dim steel and let only the sweeping arc be gold — and stop overloading gold: inspected should be ley, hovered should be gold, stunned should be its own. Then move kill stacks and chamber pips onto the model as emissive geometry driven by uGlow so they occlude correctly and read as the tower's own light.

name: Map chooser and its six thumbnails
fixDirection: Render each thumbnail once to an offscreen canvas on screen entry, then make that thumbnail an actual 3D board render (or an oblique projection of it) so the card matches 00-board-default; bank the freed per-frame cost into a card hover lift and a lit route trace.

name: road mesh and edging
fixDirection: Reverse the winding on both kerb quads in GLGeometry.road so the lift is actually visible, then add the edge treatment the palette already carries — read theme.roadEdge and theme.roadCenter and lay them in as emissive geometry on the deck (an inset rail each side and a centre trace), not as a canvas overlay. That one change buys the raised ribbon, the ley read and the direction of travel together.

name: Warbringer meshes (7 tiers: base, a3, a4, a5, b3, b4, b5)
fixDirection: Spend triangles on the man, not the hammer: roughly triple the 1368–2964 budget into apron, bracer, bare forearm and a shaped head, and re-lay the value ladder so the apron is the largest and darkest surface and the bare forearm plus the ley are the only bright notes (right now the anvil-stand steel is the brightest thing on him). That one change moves silhouette, form, material and colour together.

name: muzzle flash
fixDirection: Make the flash a light instead of a shape: one createRadialGradient disc drawn with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter', arms rotated by the tower's own aim plus a per-shot random offset, and an ease-out fade (fade^0.5) instead of the linear ramp — so a burst reads as five discharges rather than five copies of one stamp.

name: impacts (rifleman-hit, arcane-aoe, arcane-empowered-hit, covenant hit)
fixDirection: Fix the Rifleman hit first and fix it at the emission site: pass liftUl through from the bullet so the mark lands at the height the round actually struck, and stop gating particles on b5 so an ordinary hit throws sparks — a strike that produces one faint ring on the floor beside the target is the single largest gap between what the simulation did and what the player sees.

name: Range circles and cones
fixDirection: Make the reach one thing in one colour — ley cyan — and make it a ley trace rather than a wireframe: a bright thin outer edge with a soft inner falloff that eases on over ~120 ms, plus radius tick marks so distance is countable. Then conform it to board relief (sample the deck height per projected point) so it stops slicing through raised tiles.

name: Wave banner
fixDirection: Give it a body and a beat: a ley-cyan bracketed plate that wipes open from centre with an eased overshoot, gold for cleared/payout vs cyan for incoming, and hold the cleared banner in a queue instead of letting the next announce() clobber it.

name: Cash popups
fixDirection: Replace the linear rise with a fast eased pop-and-settle (scale 1.35->1.0 over ~120ms, then a decelerating drift), add a 2px dark stroke so gold survives over lit geometry, and scale the type size with the bounty so a big kill actually reads as one.

name: Arcane Sniper meshes (7 tiers: base, a3, a4, a5, b3, b4, b5)
fixDirection: Re-export a3, a4, a5 and b5 with animated groups — at minimum a breech/coil group and a recoil-and-settle — so the four tiers the player spends the most money on stop being statues that shoot. That is the single criterion scoring a 1, and it affects more than half the ladder.

name: bullet round
fixDirection: Give the round a radial falloff and an additive core: replace the two hard-edged discs with one createRadialGradient head (white core -> amber -> zero) drawn with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter', and re-add the ground shadow the 2D path had. That single change also fixes the material score for every other member of this layer, since they all share the same flat-fill idiom.

name: The four modelled enemies (normal / swarm / brute / hive)
fixDirection: Re-key the enemy palette so it reads at 20 px and stops colliding with the towers: take the brass trim off the enemies entirely (it is the towers' and the money HUD's colour), widen the body value split so plate separates from housing at play zoom, and enlarge the emissive red core area so the one-glance read at default camera is 'dark machine with a hot red slot' instead of 'gold-banded slab'.

name: Forge slam (Warbringer path A)
fixDirection: Drop the `* p0.scale * 0.5` from the crack lineWidth so the split reads at the default camera, and clip the whole mark to the impact's own `arcRadians`/`aim` the way drawStakeRing already does — a 120-degree wedge that lies about covering a circle is worse than no mark.

name: Title menu, incl. reactor and comms dish
fixDirection: Drive the reactor and dish from a clock: pulse the core's emissive ring on a slow non-linear envelope, rotate the vane ring a few degrees per second, sweep the dish and blink the console lamps out of phase. That one change moves motion 1->4 and effect 2->3 with almost no cost, and fixes the single largest gap between this screen and a shipping title screen.

name: Rifleman meshes (5 tiers: base, a3, a5, b3, b5)
fixDirection: Re-lay his value ladder so the coat and trousers stop sitting within a few percent of the board — lift the coat off black, separate the legs and the weapon from the torso mass, and give the head a jaw and brow — because at the default camera he is currently a dark smear with a red dot. Fix towerGlowTint at the same time so a tower whose emissives are fire renders as fire rather than being multiplied by ley cyan.

name: grid lines
fixDirection: Replace the extruded rails with inlaid quads at a pitch tied to something real (the 80x72 panel module the 2D floor already used), tint them from theme.panelLine rather than panelDark, and carry the same grid across the raised zone tops so decks read as fabricated plating instead of blank rectangles.

name: the B5 covenant round
fixDirection: Port the two separated rails and the crossing discharge bolt from draw-pack.js's drawCovenantRound into gl-world's version — the split-core negative space is what makes this read as a heavy round rather than a purple lozenge, and it is already written and proven in the sprite path.

name: The two recruit summons (recruit-b4, recruit-b5)
fixDirection: Capture them before doing anything else — this group was scored without a single render of it, and silhouette, material and colour are all judged from palette data rather than pixels. Then the change the palette already predicts: give each recruit one light-value surface (the B5 helmet, the B4 face-rag) so a five-colour dark-earth figure is not a black smear on a dark-teal board.

name: B5 strike and ritual circle
fixDirection: Build both light columns from camera-facing corners instead of world-X-aligned ones (offset perpendicular to the view vector, as drawCovenantHit's screen-facing seal already does) so the shaft survives an orbit — right now the whole telegraph disappears at a 90-degree camera turn.
